drivingQuestion: What does 'ועוד' in the mishna connect to?
outcomeNote: 'ועוד' marks consecutive rulings not broken by an interruption on another topic

segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara first analyzes the wording of this mishna: «What was taught» previously, «that» the tanna «teaches» in this mishna: «And furthermore» Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava said, which implies a continuation of the previous mishna?

segments.he: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּתְנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא לְחוּמְרָא וְקָתָנֵי אַחֲרִיתִי, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָתָנֵי ״וְעוֹד״ — וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּתְנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא לְחוּמְרָא וְקָתָנֵי אַחֲרִיתִי, וְלָא קָתָנֵי ״וְעוֹד״!
segments.en: «If you say» that «because he» first «taught one stringency» concerning the upright boards surrounding a well, «and» then «he teaches another» stringency about an enclosure, and «for that reason» the tanna of the mishna «teaches: And furthermore,» then there is a difficulty. «Didn’t Rabbi Yehuda» also «teach one stringency and» then «teach another» stringency, «and» yet the tanna of the mishna «does not teach: And furthermore» Rabbi Yehuda said?

segments.he: הָתָם אַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן, הָכָא לָא אַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara answers that the cases are different: «There, the Rabbis interrupted» Rabbi Yehuda’s statements in order to disagree with him, and hence it is not possible to say: And furthermore Rabbi Yehuda said. «Here,» however, «the Rabbis did not interrupt him,» as the two statements of Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava immediately follow one another.

segments.he: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּאַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן לָא קָתָנֵי ״וְעוֹד״? וְהָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּסוּכָּה, דְּאַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן, וְקָתָנֵי ״וְעוֹד״?
segments.en: The Gemara raises a difficulty: Does this mean that «wherever the» disputing «Rabbis interrupt» their colleague, the tanna «does not teach: And furthermore? But» with regard to «Rabbi Eliezer» in a mishna «in» tractate «Sukka» (27a), «where the Rabbis interrupted his» statements, nonetheless the tanna «teaches: And furthermore.»

segments.he: הָתָם, בְּמִילְּתֵיהּ הוּא דְּאַפְסְקוּהּ. הָכָא, בְּמִילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי אַפְסְקוּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: It is not the same; «there, they interrupted» Rabbi Eliezer «with» a ruling with regard to «his» own «topic; here,» however, «they interrupted» Rabbi Yehuda with a ruling with regard to «an» altogether «different matter.» Consequently, his first statement had already been forgotten, and it is not the Mishna’s style to join together statements where the sequential link between them has already been severed.
